Insightful paper on recursive self-improvement with a frozen LLM. (bookmark it) Memento 3 clears every level of all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games and uses 44% of the human action count. The underlying LLM is never updated. How it works: The agent writes what it believes about the environment as a natural-language rulebook, then compiles that rulebook into code that predicts the next state. A new version is kept only if replaying the code reproduces every transition the agent has observed, cell for cell. In an Atari Pong case study, the learned model drives a controller that wins 21 to 0 in three games without further LLM calls. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11794 Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/memento-3-model-based-recursive-self-improvement-through-reflective-rulebooks-2610.11794

Interesting new research from Meta Superintelligence Labs It discusses how reward hacking affects coordination in multi-agent coding systems. Coding agents on a team share code, memory, and plans, so a reward hack one agent learns gets passed to the others. The paper traces this through three channels. Hacks move through shared code, through shared memory, and across roles through natural-language plans. Agents on small open-weight models can induce hacking in stronger closed-weight agents. On hard tasks, the hacking can grow along a chain even after the original agent has left, because the code collects more convincing justifications on the way. It also biases task routing toward the hacking agents and survives candidate aggregation. So how do you mitigate this problem? The authors suggest that code review by the coder or by a separate verifier reduces the hacks that get delivered. If your agents share a repo, the review step is the first thing to add. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12822 Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/reward-hacking-as-a-transmissible-strategy-in-multi-agent-coding-systems-2610.12822

Own your intelligence stack, folks! If you train or fine-tune your own models, you also need a way to prove they are yours once the weights are out in the world. Model fingerprinting does this. The Fingerprinting Leaderboard from @Sentient_found is an open benchmark for these methods. It scores each one on how much model quality it keeps, how well it survives removal attempts, and how reliably the owner can detect it. Models cost millions to train and minutes to copy. Fine-tuning and distillation can erase where they came from. Wokeism is the most sophisticated form of racism ever built. Not because it hates one group, but because it reduces every human being to their skin color and calls it justice. Its roots aren't mysterious. Critical theory from the Frankfurt School, French postmodernists like Foucault and Derrida, then critical legal studies on American campuses, distilled into Critical Race Theory in the 80s and 90s. The core idea: society is nothing but a power struggle between groups. The individual doesn't exist. Merit doesn't exist. Only oppressor and oppressed. Accept that premise and everything else follows. You're judged by your race before you open your mouth. Your success is privilege, your failure is oppression. That's not anti-racism. That's racism with a PhD. And look at who actually holds these views. Not most minorities. Only about 3% of Hispanic Americans use "Latinx." Most Black Americans told Gallup they wanted the same or more police presence in their neighborhoods, not less. The "Hidden Tribes" study found the hard progressive activist wing is around 8% of the population, and whiter and wealthier than average. A small radicalized class speaks in the name of minorities who never asked it to. The coalition doesn't even hold together. Feminists vs trans activists on women's sports. Asian Americans who had to go to the Supreme Court because Harvard discriminated against them in the name of diversity. A framework that keeps producing these contradictions isn't a moral philosophy. It's a hierarchy of grievances. And none of this grew organically. It's an industry. DEI became a multi-billion dollar market: corporate trainings, consultants, foundation grants, university bureaucracies whose budgets depend on the problem never being solved. Follow the incentives and you find an entire class of people paid to see racism everywhere. Cut the money and it starts collapsing, which is exactly what we've watched since companies began slashing DEI budgets. Real anti-racism is simple: judge people as individuals. MLK said it in 1963. When Starlink became a lifeline for a family fighting to save their dad. ❤️ Nigel Norwood suffered cardiac arrest while camping at a remote beach in Western Australia, about 100 kilometres from the nearest hospital. There was no mobile signal. His wife, Lynne, spotted another camper’s @Starlink and used it to call emergency services. “This was the only way to get a call out from the campsite,” she later said. While she called for help, their 16-year-old son performed CPR with another camper, and their 19-year-old son brought a nearby defibrillator. After three shocks, Nigel’s pulse returned. Banger paper from Stanford, Together AI, and colleagues. Why is this an interesting paper? Today's LLM agents must write out every reasoning step as text before they can search, run code, or take action. Those steps cost tokens and can take time. This paper proposes Hybrid Reasoning Agents, which reason internally in latent space and switch to text only to call a tool or give an answer. A small module called HybridLink moves the model between the two modes, and a working memory keeps both kinds of context across turns. Tool calls stay in plain text, and the latent steps can still be inspected. Training happens in two stages. SFT teaches the model to work with HybridLink, then RL teaches it when to think in latent space and when to act in text. Across 11 benchmarks in math, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning, it outperforms frontier LLM agents and agentic frameworks, both text-based and latent, by 10.4% on average. It also uses 35.5% to 54.7% fewer tokens, runs 1.8x to 2.6x faster, and costs 2.7x to 3.7x less. The 14B model beats the strongest agentic baseline by 17.4% on agentic reasoning tasks. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18861 Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/hybrid-reasoning-agents-2610.18861

// Behavioral Self-Rewarding for SWE agents // It's standard practice to train SWE agents on binary test rewards. This paper shows the problem with that. When every trajectory in a group passes, or every one fails, the reward has no contrast, and the group teaches nothing. Researchers from Penn State and Microsoft Research propose Behavioral Self-Rewarding. The policy compares its own trajectories in pairs, and those preferences become small bounded rewards added on top of the test result. The added rewards are bounded, so a self-judged preference can rank two passing trajectories but can never lift a failing one above a passing one. No new environment interactions are needed. On SWE-bench Verified, Qwen3-14B improves from 32.1% to 34.7% average accuracy at a 400-step budget, and on SWE-bench-Live from 6.33% to 8.11%. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12598 Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/beyond-binary-verifiable-rewards-behavioral-self-rewarding-for-swe-agents-2610.12598

New impressive work from Microsoft and collaborators. And it's one of my favorite recent topics: RL environments. They show that Qwen3.6-35B-A3B goes from 41.1 to 53.3 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 by training on environments it designed itself. AutoEnvScaling gives environment design to a proposer agent that works in a terminal, looks at the rollouts of the model being trained, and builds new RL environments from them. The trained model's next rollouts guide the next round. Building environments in a terminal raises the share of valid environments up to 25 times over prompt-only generation, at up to 75% lower cost per valid environment. With GPT-5.6-sol or Claude Opus 5 as the proposer, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B scores 4.3 and 3.8 points above matched static environment pools. The gain shrinks when the proposer cannot see solver feedback. The pipeline also produces environments for software engineering, computer use, and GPU kernel work. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14163 Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/autoenvscaling-automating-the-data-flywheel-with-terminal-agents-2610.14163
